subject.title: Model configuration accepts unvalidated model names, enabling silent misconfiguration

question: Should OpenClaw warn, fail validation, or only doctor-report configured model refs that resolve syntactically but are absent from the trusted runtime catalog?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but AGENTS.md and VISION.md make config strictness, forward-compatible custom models, and fallback behavior compatibility-sensitive enough that automation should not choose the permanent policy alone.

options.title: Warn in doctor/config validate
options.body: Surface catalog-missing configured refs as warnings with clear paths and hints while preserving forward-compatible custom model setups.

options.title: Fail config validation
options.body: Reject unknown configured refs early, reducing runtime failures but risking breakage for custom or not-yet-catalogued models.

options.title: Limit to doctor only
options.body: Keep runtime/config writes permissive and use doctor as the advisory repair surface, accepting that misconfiguration may still reach runtime until users run doctor.

recommendation.title: Warn in doctor/config validate
recommendation.body: Surface catalog-missing configured refs as warnings with clear paths and hints while preserving forward-compatible custom model setups.

likelyOwner.reason: The model config and selection design history points to this owner for the policy choice.
